sentences.text: The petitioner purchased the said plot and the transfer was permitted by the respondent  authority.
It is no doubt true that when the purchase was made and the transfer was  permitted, the purpose shown was to establish an electronic industry.
It is the case of the  petitioner that the petitioner has experience of processing of frozen foods and is in such a  business since almost a decade or so.

The learned advocate for the petitioner has  taken this Court through the no objection certificate issued by the Regional Manager of  respondent authority dated 4.7.2016 as well as circular of the respondent Corporation dated 11.3.2013.

The permissions granted by Gandhinagar Municipal  Corporation, Food Safety and Standard Authority of India as well as Gujarat Pollution Control  B o a r d h a v e g r a n t e d c o n s e n t t o e s t a b l i s h w h i c h i s p o p u l a r l y c a l l e d  and known as no objection certificate in exercise of powers conferred under Section 25 of

. The respondent HC-NIC Page 2 of 5 Created On Sun Aug 13 04:39:44 IST 2017 has filed a reply to the averments and  contentions raised in the petition and relying upon the policy decision vide circular dated  13.11.2013, it has been contended by the respondent that the applications filed for  permission to establish nonelectronic and non polluting units would be scrutinized by the

S c r e e n i n g C o m m i t t e e f o r a l l o t m e n t w h i c h i s t o  be stationed by GIDC at Gandhinagar and based upon the report of such Committee, final  decision has been vested with the Vice Chairman and Managing Director of the GIDC.
It is also  contended that such Committee shall consist of an officer from Gujarat Pollution Control Board as  member of such Committee.

In light of the policy decision of the respondent C o r p o r a t i o n d a t e d 1 3 . 1 1 . 2 0 1 3 , i t i s c r y s t a l c l e a r t h a t e v e n  in electronic estate in order to see that the industrial development continues and exist even in a  specialized zone, other industries are also to be permitted.
However, there has to be strict  compliance of the conditions which are attached with the circular dated 13.11.2013.

5. Without expressing any opinion on merits as observed hereinabove and as the  record of the petition indicates all necessary and primary permissions such as food and  safety, licence from the local authority to establish a particular business and more  particularly HC-NIC Page 3 of 5 Created On Sun Aug 13 04:39:44 IST 2017 consent of Gujarat
Pollution Control Board
is also obtained by the petitioner under the provisions of the  Water Act, 1974 as well as Air Act, 1981.
On bare reading of the policy declaration  by the respondentCorporation
by its circular dated 13.11.2013, it appears that  prima facie the petitioner has placed on record at least before this Court all necessary  permissions.

The circular dated 13.11.2013 nowhere provides that consent of the  association is to be taken and on bare reading of the order dated 4.7.2016 which is impugned  in this petition what is mainly waived with the authority of the respondentCorporation is the  opinion expressed by the association which, in opinion of this Court, is de hors the policy of  the respondentCorporation.

6. In light of the aforesaid therefore, the decision dated 4.7.2016 is hereby quashed  and set aside and the application dated 12.5.2016 filed by the petitioner before the  respondent authority stands revived.
